extracted.intended_audience: aspiring comedy writers and readers looking for books and resources on comedy writing and performance
extracted.subtask_description: A Goodreads catalogue page listing and describing books about comedy writing (books on joke-writing, stand-up, sketch, sitcoms, improv, and the business of comedy), including user-supplied quotes that state craft principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comedic character, joke formulas, and practical performance/business skills
rubrics_metrics.description: Covers: 1-Discovering your Comedic Character; 2- an 80-page workbook using the best joke formulas from over 25 years in my workshops; 3- How to put it all together, deal with audiences, clubs, and the biz.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verbatim quote from a book blurb (Steve North, How to Kill in Comedy). Implies a multi-part approach to learning comedy: develop a distinctive comedic persona, learn and practice proven joke formulas via exercises/workbook material, and gain practical skills for performing and navigating the comedy industry (audiences, clubs, business).

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on being an honest, good writer rather than only trying to be funnier
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't concentrate on becoming a better humor writer, just concentrate on being the best writer that you can become. If you're funny, the work will end up being funny. And if you're not funny, the work will still end up being good. Concentrate on being the most honest writer you can be, and let everything else follow--because it will.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verbatim quote (John Hodgman). Advice emphasizes craft and honesty over chasing humor as a separate skill—prioritize strong writing and authenticity, which will often produce humor as a byproduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learn specific short-form and TV comedy formats (monologue jokes, desk pieces, sketches, parodies, remotes)
rubrics_metrics.description: How to write monologue jokes, desk pieces, sketches, parodies, audience pieces, remotes, and other short-form comedy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Taken from the subtitle of 'Comedy Writing for Late-Night TV' (Joe Toplyn). Functions as a checklist of short-form and late-night comedy formats a writer should learn to write for that medium.

rubrics_metrics.name: Think, write, perform, and monetize comedy
rubrics_metrics.description: How to Think Funny, Write Funny, Act Funny, And Get Paid For It.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subtitle of 'Comedy Writing Secrets' (Melvin Helitzer). Lays out four interrelated dimensions of a comedy career: idea-generation (thinking funny), crafting material (writing funny), delivery/performance (acting funny), and career/business aspects (getting paid).
